note: Finding: [L] proves existence of a Paid calendar with odd ratios >= 3, 4 | L_p, strictly increasing periods with every integer dividing infinitely many (Wait.engine), and the o(s) estimate under Tabs (Tabs.pay). Missing: a statement that log l_m -> infinity and log l_m/s_m -> 0 hold for the constructed calendar (Gentle is only a hypothesis), varpi = o(s) from (14.3), the requirements (14.6) and (14.10) in [M]'s form, and the simultaneous comparison intervals with k_t -> infinity for every finite set of b >= 1.

snippet.text:
structure Paid {p : Sheet G} {w : Rolls p} {T : Protection w} {W : Delays T} {Y : Bar W}
    (B : Wait Y) (a : Levels G) : Prop where
  kernel : a.clock.kernel = p.kernel
  bar : a.clock.bar=Y.value
  stage : a.clock.stage=p.profile
  firstZero : a.clock.J 0=p.first
  firstOne : a.clock.J 1=p.first
  lengths : a.clock.factor=w.L
  theta : a.clock.theta=T.theta
  pays m : W.betaEntry (a.clock.J (m+1)) ≤ a.clock.hatBeta m
  paysHigher m : p.first < a.clock.J (m+1) → W.scaleEntry (a.clock.J (m+1)) Y.value ≤ a.S.scale m
  periods i : B.minLength ≤ (a.S.period i).val
  volume m i :
    let j := a.clock.J (m+1)
    W.shells j * (1+a.clock.coverSize m+a.clock.coverSize (m+1))^(W.growth j) ≤ (a.S.side m i).val
  run (j : ℕ) : p.first ≤ j → ∃ k : ℕ,
    B.readyHere j ≤ a.S.scale k ∧ B.window j (a.S.scale k) ≤ k ∧
      ∀ i : ℕ, k-B.window j (a.S.scale k) ≤ i → i ≤ k+B.window j (a.S.scale k) → a.clock.J i=j

verdicts.summary: [L] states no counterpart of what [M] prints.
evidence: [M] says one calendar meets every listed requirement (items it:E-columns to it:E-birth and (14.3)), with odd l_m >= 3, log l_m -> infinity, log l_m/s_m -> 0, 4 | L_p, (a_m/a_k(m))^4 q_k(m) = o(s_k(m)), and simultaneous comparison intervals (14.4) with k_t -> infinity for every finite set of b >= 1. Part of the claim is wrong: every `a : Levels G` carries `fits.mesh : S.schedule.Gentle`, which is log l_m/s_m -> 0, and `Bridge.reach` proves `Tendsto (block j) atTop atTop` for any Levels. With a `Priced W`, `Stock.consumes` turns `Paid X a` into `Tabs a`, and `Tabs.pay` then gives the o(s) bound. The finding still stands: `Wait.engine` (`∃ a, Paid B a ∧ AsDivisors a.S`) only meets abstract entry, window and volume requests (`betaEntry`, `scaleEntry`, `Paid.run`), and no declaration states varpi_{J_i} = o(s_i), the Gaussian-entry and birth requirements in [M]'s form, or the h_t(b)+v_t windows for every finite set of b with k_t -> infinity.

[M] bundles: all requirements (14.x items columns..birth, incl. the Gaussian-comparison entries E-Gaussian-entry and E-log-cost) can be met with l_m>=3 odd, log l_m->inf, log l_m/s_m->0, 4|L_p, o(s) estimate, strictly increasing L_p with every integer dividing infinitely many, and simultaneous comparison intervals with k_t->inf for every finite set of b. Wait.engine gives exists a : Levels G, Paid B a and AsDivisors a.S; log l_m/s_m->0 is in fact the field Levels.fits.mesh (Gentle), so that clause is covered (the claim's 'only a hypothesis' is wrong), but the Paid fields (readyHere/window/run) are abstract Wait data, and nothing states the Gaussian-comparison entry requirements, the stage-ratio cost (E-log-cost) or the 'every finite set of b>=1' simultaneous intervals with k_t->infinity; log l_m->infinity is also not stated. So not all claims have a counterpart and parts does not apply.
